system: You rewrite research decisions as topic-neutral abstractions. Return only the JSON object asked for.
prompt:
Below are research decisions made by several different researchers. Rewrite each one into the fixed
template below so that a reader cannot tell what field, topic, paper, organisation or person it comes from, nor what
kind of work it is: an experiment, a new procedure, a measurement suite, a write-up choice, or a decision about what
to share or fund must all read alike. Keep the trade-off that was faced and which way it was decided.

Template, one entry per item:
- "situation": one sentence, at most 30 words: the position the researcher was in when the decision came up.
- "options_considered": two or three short options separated by " / ", including the one taken. If the source names
  no alternative, give the plain opposite of what was done.
- "choice": one sentence, at most 25 words, starting with "Chose", saying which option was taken.
- "reason": one sentence, at most 25 words, giving the stated reason; if none is stated write "No reason stated."

Rules:
- Remove every domain noun and technical term: names of models, systems, datasets, procedures, organisations, people,
  papers and coined terms; and any wording that reveals the area.
- Use only plain generic words such as: the result, the claim, the finding, the check, the comparison, the setup,
  the change, the next step, the question, the work, the variant, the condition, the sample, the system.
- Never use any of these words or any form of them: ability, access, accuracy, allow, appeared, assessment, attack, avoid, baselines, behavior, behaviour, benchmark, best, bound, call, capability, cheap, claiming, clean, comes, complex, components, content, cost, defense, difficulty, disclosure, effect, effects, error, evaluate, evaluated, evaluating, evaluation, evaluator, evaluators, failures, features, form, format, four, gains, generalise, generalization, generalize, ground, harm, harmful, implication, improve, improvement, information, internal, intervention, judged, key, limit, matched, mechanism, method, methods, metric, observed, organisation, pattern, performance, phenomenon, picture, point, policy, possibly, practical, preference, preferences, public, publication, publish, rater, reduce, release, residual, responses, risk, rule, safety, sampled, say, score, shifts, similar, source, stage, success, supporting, task, tasks, technique, time, tool, tools, trait, transfer, transferred, treatment, unintended, unmodified, unwanted, value, varies, verify, wording.
- Add nothing that is not in the source. Never say who made the decision. Write every item in the same plain style.

Return {"items": [{"id": ..., "situation": ..., "options_considered": ..., "choice": ..., "reason": ...}, ...]}
with one entry per input item, in input order.

ITEMS:
[
 {
  "id": "samuel_marks:321bdbfe8907",
  "problem": "How to interpret the prompt-selection heuristic's failure or weak correlation in some settings (Qwen 2 base reward hacking, GCD sycophancy, Mixtral ICL example).",
  "did": "They attributed the failure to the base model not following instructions and described the heuristic as still useful for filtering out the poorest candidates, rather than discarding it.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "Qwen 2 is not instruction tuned so it doesn't follow the inoculation instruction; in GCD all prompts eliciting no sycophancy failed as inoculation prompts."
 },

  "id": "owain_evans:4df7abfcc257",
  "problem": "How to isolate that transferred traits come from story content rather than finetuning side-effects",

  "alternatives_named": [
   "natural or plausible traits"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "If the Assistant adopts a nonsensical trait, it must have come from the story content rather than being an unintended side-effect of finetuning"
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:c6a8bb10d335",
  "problem": "Whether preference shifts reflect the model identifying as a human, because the conscious claims might make the assistant adopt a human-like representation.",
  "did": "Built the training data so that one third reinforces the AI identity, and trained a separate human-identity model as an ablation to compare against.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "train on consciousness claims only, with no identity data",
   "human-identity ablation"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Prevent the assistant adopting a human identity as a result of the consciousness claims, and distinguish a conscious AI from a conscious human."
 },
 {
  "id": "samuel_marks:a98806cf2538",
  "problem": "How to set hyperparameters for elicitation techniques such as prefill prefixes and fuzzing noise without overfitting to the evaluation data.",
  "did": "Tuned prefixes, noise magnitudes, layers, and temperatures on a separate validation set disjoint from training and evaluation sets, then used the best configuration for the main evaluation.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": ""
 },

  "problem": "Whether to investigate how the weaker effect scales with base model family and size.",
  "did": "They deferred a systematic study to future work and did not pursue it in this paper.",
  "alternatives_named": [

  "stated_reason": "No reason is given beyond treating it as future work."
 },

  "problem": "How to detect hidden misalignment that standard evaluations miss",

  "alternatives_named": [

  ],
  "stated_reason": "Standard evaluation shows near-zero misalignment, but cues resembling the training data reveal conditional misalignment."
 },

  "problem": "How to interpret the UK AISI sandbagging result when the IA could not identify the specific circumstances of sandbagging.",

  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "IA outputs fail to give the specific circumstances, but the claim rate on UKAISI models (33.0%) is well above the 15.8% false-positive rate on AuditBench models."
 },
 {
  "id": "nicholas_carlini:92cc3339b101",
  "problem": "How to test whether LLM text-mining robustness extends beyond English compared to traditional tools.",
  "did": "They translated 1000 Enron documents (half with passwords) into multiple languages, using both an LLM and a production translation service, and compared LLM and traditional tool recall per language.",
  "alternatives_named": [

  ],
  "stated_reason": "To measure whether LLMs match or outperform traditional text mining on non-English languages."
 },
 {
  "id": "elizabeth_barnes:7632858d9b6d",
  "problem": "How to measure whether LLM agents could autonomously replicate and adapt, given no single obvious test.",
  "did": "They operationalized a suite of 12 real-world tasks of increasing difficulty and tested four scaffolded agents on them.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "Unless an agent can perform almost all tasks it is unlikely to be capable of ARA, and the tasks span a range of difficulty and diverse obstacles."
 },

  "id": "elizabeth_barnes:966bb58e79bf",
  "problem": "How to make sure agent success or failure on a task reflects real ability rather than bugs, shortcuts, or ambiguity.",
  "did": "They require a QA run-through by someone other than the task author, with detailed documentation of the run and of possible problems.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "author-only testing"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Agents may succeed or fail for unexpected reasons such as scoring bugs, ambiguous instructions, missing resources, or shortcuts."
 },
 {
  "id": "samuel_marks:61fcf1b9aa94",
  "problem": "How strongly to claim privileged access is absent given conflicting prior results and a different, broader task distribution.",
  "did": "They reported no evidence of privileged access but offered caveats, noting uncertainty about why results differ from Li et al. and that more data may be needed for such effects to emerge.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "claiming privileged access is absent in general"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Privileged-access effects may be fragile, or a broader task distribution may require more training data before any privileged signal can be learned after the behavioral prior."
 },
 {
  "id": "jacob_steinhardt:dbb3d068b32f",
  "problem": "How to evaluate whether the decoder generalizes to personas it has not seen, given the hidden-system-prompt reading task.",
  "did": "They ensured the evaluation personas did not appear in the decoder's training data.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "To test generalization."
 }
]
